Question Paper  
Exam Date & Time: 19-Nov-2025 (02:00 PM - 05:00 PM)  
  
  
  MANIPAL ACADEMY OF HIGHER EDUCATION  
  
  FIFTH SEMESTER B.TECH. DEGREE EXAMINATIONS - NOVEMBER 2025  
  SUBJECT: ECE 3121/ECE_3121 ANALOG AND DIGITAL COMMUNICATION  
  (SPL: ELECTRONICS & COMMUNICATION ENGINEERING)  
  ANALOG AND DIGITAL COMMUNICATION [ECE 3121]  
Marks: 50                                                                                                                                 Duration: 180 mins.  
  
  A  
Answer all the questions.  
Missing data may be suitably assumed.  
  
1A)               With relevant mathematical expressions and block diagram explain the working of switching modulator for AM generation.             (5)  
  Mention the specification of filter to be used to obtain the desired AM signal.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO1" / Cognitive Level: "Understand"  
  
1B)               Write down the expression for NBFM signal. Given a maximum frequency deviation 1 kHz and a highest modulating frequency 5          (3)  
  kHz, with       . Compute the modulation index and the FM bandwidth for this condition.  
  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO1" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
1C)               Determine the Fourier Transform of the signal                                                                                      (2)  
  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO1" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
2A)                                                                                                                                                  (5)  
  
  
  Determine orthonormal basis functions using Gram-Schmidt and express the signals in terms of these basis functions. Sketch the  
  resulting orthonormal functions.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
2B)               Illustrate how the matched filter impulse response is obtained as a time-reversed and delayed version of the input signal. Apply   (3)  
  $$this property to explain why the output is maximized at t = T.$$  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Understand"  
  
2C)                                                                                                                                                        (2)  
  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Understand"  
  
  Page #1

3A)                   With the help of a neat block diagram, describe the duo-binary conversion system. Obtain the frequency response of duo-binary     (5)  
  encoder and hence derive the impulse response. Also plot the magnitude and phase responses of the system.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO2" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
3B)                   Consider the 4-bit binary sequence "1100". Obtain the discrete PAM representation of the sequence using RZ unipolar format.       (3)  
  Calculate the autocorrelation function of the RZ unipolar format assuming that the input data is statistically independent and  
  equally likely.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO2" / Cognitive Level: "Understand"  
  
3C)                   Sketch the typical eye pattern and describe Inter-symbol Interference performance parameters.                                     (2)  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO2" / Cognitive Level: "Understand"  
  
4A)                   Derive the expression for average probability of error at the receiver for a binary-encoded PCM wav that uses nonreturn-to-zero   (5)  
  unipolar (ON-OFF) format, assuming AWGN channel. Plot the corresponding signal space diagram with decision boundary and  
  likelihood functions.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO2" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
4B)                                                                                                                                                           (3)  
  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
4C)                   The binary data sequence 1 0 1 1 0 0 1 0 0 is applied to the input of a DPSK transmitter. Determine the differentially encoded    (2)  
  sequence and transmitted phase. Assume initial reference bit as 1.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
5A)                   Construct minimum variance Huffman code for the given source probabilities pk =[0.12, 0.11, 0.41, 0.19, 0.17]. Also determine the (5)  
  average code length of this Huffman code.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO5" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
5B)                   Determine the entropy, efficiency and redundancy of the Huffman code as given in Q5A.                                             (3)  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO5" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
5C)                   Determine the minimum variance of this Huffman code as given in Q5A.                                                              (2)  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO5" / Cognitive Level: "Application"
